lines.text: 'When Truth and Virtue have to do with thee,
lines.meaning: When Truth and Virtue, meaning honest and good people, have dealings with you, Opportunity,

lines.text: A thousand crosses keep them from thy aid:
lines.meaning: a thousand obstacles (crosses) stand between them and your help.

lines.text: They buy thy help; but Sin ne'er gives a fee,
lines.meaning: Good people have to pay for your help, but Sin never pays you anything.

lines.text: He gratis comes; and thou art well appaid
lines.meaning: Sin comes free of charge, and you are perfectly pleased (well appaid) with that,

lines.text: As well to hear as grant what he hath said.
lines.meaning: just as happy to hear what Sin asks as to grant it.

lines.text: My Collatine would else have come to me
lines.meaning: Otherwise my husband Collatine would have come to me

lines.text: When Tarquin did, but he was stay'd by thee.
lines.meaning: at the moment Tarquin did, but you delayed (stay'd) Collatine.

summary: Opportunity, when honest and good people have dealings with you, a thousand obstacles keep them from your help. They have to pay for it, but Sin never pays you anything. Sin comes free of charge and you are perfectly pleased with that, just as happy to hear what Sin asks as to grant it. Otherwise my husband Collatine would have come to me at the moment Tarquin did, but you delayed him.
